No. No. Absolutely not. No.

If you want a vacuum there's much much much easier ways to make it besides going to space. You can draw a much better vacuum here with cheap parts than you'd have in space anyway, or you could just create an inert environment using non-reactive gas if you're just trying to mitigate oxidation. That's like going to the North Poll because you discovered something useful about ice.

However, what's more interesting in that field is a machine that produces a vacuum or other inert environment (argon gas shielding) and then deposits and bonds powdered non-oxidized metal layers. The field is called additive manufacturing. The experimental selective laser melting machines that I have worked with do this by layering a very thin coat of powder over a surface and heating exactly where you want bonded with a very fast scanning laser. The process repeats with a new layer and you can produce an arbitrary metal part in the same manner your printer produces an arbitrary picture on paper.

I'm guessing your girlfriend has a laptop, and the hard drive in said laptop is ~3 years old. All laptops do that, and unless you buy a new hard drive, it's going to be slow regardless of what OS you put on it.

Laptops have troubles properly dispersing heat which drastically shortens the life time of hard drives (depending on use) which are very sensitive to heat over extended periods of times. That's why companies put so much money and effort into keeping the temperature in data centers at about 21 degrees.
